clue: Two pin-jointed elders between twin trees

atlas.why: fixed stage: one profile figure bracketed by two trees over a ground strip; take the bracketed staging only
same stage with changed blocking: trees and ground hold, only the figures change, which is the row's rule

takes.seen: 0-2.5 s cockpit matches the master (six-bolt port with chip at two o'clock, hinge, latch, ballast slot, chalk chart, toggle, amber lamp, dent on the right wall) with the twin spotted trunks alone in the port; at about 0.9 s a grey ball weight hangs beside a turkey tail fan at the left edge and by 1.7 s it sits in the ballast slot; 2.7-5 s push-in, the two pin-jointed elders in waistcoats stand on the mossy bank between the trunks with the carved boundary stone lower right, as in the still; at about 4.0-5.0 s each raises one stiff arm from the shoulder pin (toll gate); at about 5.5-6.3 s both have turned to face each other in profile while trunks, bank and stone have not moved; a faint reddish turkey reflection sits lower left on the glass throughout the push-in; at about 6.6 s a cross-dissolve (the outside porthole with Turkey shows through the elders) leads to the outside view at 7-8 s: riveted metal tin on pebbles, Turkey behind the amber port, two speckled trout at left looking in

open: outside view (7-8 s) has no boundary stone, no elders and no twin trunks: the tin is not beside the stone, nobody points or offers a coin, so neither of Trout's readings (boundary-stone thief / new ferryboat) is staged; the still at least holds trout, stone and elders in one frame
the cut across the glass is a cross-dissolve at about 6.6 s, not a hard cut at 5.5 s, leaving about 1.3 s outside
the elders turn to profile but stay full-width figures; they never become paper-thin edges, so the 'paper cutouts' reading rests only on the brass pin joints and the stiff arm swing
the trout that crosses in front of the elders in the still is absent from the port view (beat 2)

a turkey tail fan, not just a wing tip, enters at the left edge in beat 1; it stays at the edge and the room remains readable, but no wing is seen releasing the weight (the ball is simply in the air, then in the slot)
the tin does not visibly settle after the weight drops
two trout outside instead of one; Turkey is shown whole body with legs and fan in the port
the rule reads in beat 2 only (bank fixed, figures change); no new mark is made on the bank in the outside view
boundary stone carries carved glyph-like marks (inherited from the still), not readable words; no other stray text seen
